correctness.rationale: The Minkowski functional is max(|u|+|v|/sqrt3,2|v|/sqrt3) after inverse rotation. Reflection and quarter-turn of the lattice and sixth-turn of the hexagon reduce angles to [0,pi/12]. Two explicit points p_A and p_B within the fundamental triangular half-square are at distance exactly branch A or B from 0,e1,e2 in their respective regimes, with crossover tan(theta)=(4-sqrt3)/13. A triangle-cover lemma follows by tiling each triangle with six subtriangles whose vertices are original corners, edge midpoints and the common intersection witness, all lying in some convex translates. Central reflection covers the other half-square. For the reverse bound, a supporting linear form controls e1+e2 and every noncorner lattice point is Euclidean distance >=1 from a witness, greater than the candidate radius <1. Trigonometric monotonicity gives the unique cusp minimum. Independent 181x181 square-grid lower estimates at 5 angles agree with formulas within 0.015; that diagnostic is not the universal proof.

final_claim: For a circumradius-one regular hexagon rotated against Z^2, the exact all-plane covering radius on 0<=theta<=pi/12 is max(A(theta),B(theta)), where A=((sqrt(3)+1)cos+(1-sqrt(3))sin)/(2sqrt(3)) and B=((sqrt(3)+2)cos+sin)/(3sqrt(3)); unique reduced-angle minimizer theta=atan((4-sqrt(3))/13), minimum sqrt((11+6sqrt(3))/39), and known maximum 1/(3-sqrt(3)).
